text: Mera's PRF lets one passkey mint unlimited, isolated keys. Hourglass uses a second salt, separate from the wallet, as your machine identity.
From that compute namespace, we derive two keys: an SSH key that is authorized on the machines you rent, and an encryption key that providers seal your access details to.
I redeem an hour for a machine. The passkey derives the SSH key, and only its public half is committed onchain.
The provider encrypts the connection details to my sealing key and posts them onchain. Unlocking re-derives the key and decrypts them, right here in the browser.
Now I wipe all site storage and sign in again. The same passkey reproduces the exact same SSH key, and decrypts the same onchain access. Nothing was ever stored.
And it's a real key. In our end to end test, a freshly provisioned container accepts a login with the passkey-derived key, and refuses any other key.
One passkey: your account, your SSH identity, and the key your machines are sealed to.
